subject: language-tree-hub

summary: Agents should restrict graph traversal by edition_id, project_id, subject, route_id and task_id, crossing branches only when abstraction or association requires it.

subject: logic
title: Engineering use of argument analysis
summary: When an agent must judge whether a plan is valid, it first separates claim, reason, evidence, hidden premise and counterexample.

subject: logic
title: Logical precheck before tool use
summary: Before calling a tool, check goal, premise, schema, scope, side effects and validation method; missing premises block execution.

subject: logic
title: Failure diagnosis logic
summary: Separate observed facts from guesses, list candidate causes, run minimal distinguishing tests, and write reusable lessons to negative FAME routes.

subject: logic
title: Knowledge authoring consistency
summary: New knowledge must align subject level, abstraction level, source license, detail location and FAME rationale to avoid structural drift.

subject: mathematics
title: Lightweight modeling steps
summary: Translate a problem into variables, assumptions, relations, objective and validation method before applying formulas.

subject: mathematics
title: Graph traversal goal gate
summary: Limit scope first, drill down through contains edges, associate laterally through association edges, and control expansion with FAME, risk and context budget.

subject: mathematics
title: Evidence-driven parameter update
summary: Use tests, tool outputs and human feedback to update FAME parameters; retain failures for delta, risk and rho adjustments.

subject: mathematics
title: Route scoring and optimization
summary: Rank candidate routes by usefulness, fit, evidence strength, operability, association value, reuse stability, risk and context cost.

subject: computer-science
title: Knowledge graph boundary
summary: The graph stores structure, routes, sources, summaries and index refs; long content, assets and logs live in databases or external stores.

subject: computer-science
title: Specification to test
summary: Turn an engineering task into observable behavior, acceptance criteria and test commands, then preserve evidence after execution.

subject: computer-science
title: Knowledge graph and indexing engineering
summary: Large projects need light graph structure plus strong indexes: subject, alias, semantic, route_id and project_id scoping.

subject: computer-science
title: Agent project memory loop
summary: Store goal, plan, action contract, tool result, failure signature, test evidence and resume point as project overlay memory.

subject: computer-science
title: Open-source release gate
summary: Before publishing, check license, source registration, secret/path leakage, docs, tests, package artifacts and residual risk.

subject: agent-tooling
title: ProposedAction fields
summary: A mutating tool call must declare action_id, project_id, task_id, routes, tool, operation, scope, args, risk, validation and rollback.

subject: agent-tooling
title: Action template selection
summary: Choose templates by operation type and risk: read-only, structured edit, test/build, network download or destructive filesystem.

subject: agent-tooling

summary: The gateway blocks unknown tools, requires ProposedAction for mutations, requires ApprovedAction for high risk, and requires summaries after execution.

subject: agent-tooling
title: Tool result summary
summary: Every tool call writes a short evidence-backed summary with status, errors, next steps and FAME update candidates.

subject: powershell-safety
title: Filesystem mutation safety
summary: Resolve absolute paths and verify they remain inside the intended root before recursive delete or move.

subject: powershell-safety
title: PowerShell command review flow
summary: Review command, parameters, pipeline, working directory, target path, streams and side effects before execution.

subject: powershell-safety
title: Environment variable scope
summary: Distinguish process, user and machine environment variables and avoid persisting secrets accidentally.

subject: language-tree-hub
title: Multi-path lateral association
summary: For open tasks, generate multiple route candidates and keep only those with validation hooks and acceptable context cost.

subject: language-tree-hub
title: Abstraction transfer landing
summary: Lift a concrete problem to methods and subjects, transfer a verifiable structure, then return to an executable action.

subject: agent-tooling
title: Reflection iteration and failure write-back
summary: Failures produce a compact reflection, a normalized signature, a minimal validation step and FAME update candidates.

subject: agent-tooling
title: Agent usability evaluation
summary: Evaluate tool success, context savings, failure recurrence reduction, route hit rate and manual correction rate.

subject: language-tree-hub
title: Lexical semantic relations
summary: Synonym, hypernym, part-whole and related-term relations help map user words into canonical route anchors.

subject: language-tree-hub
title: Grammar dependency and operation frame
summary: Grammar parsing extracts operation, object, constraint and expected result before tool routing.

subject: language-tree-hub
title: Intent classification to route
summary: Classify user requests into planning, authoring, tool execution, debugging, evaluation or release routes.

subject: language-tree-hub
title: Minimal sufficient context pack
summary: A healthy context pack contains summaries, refs and necessary evidence, not full logs or full graph dumps.

subject: language-tree-hub
title: Association guardrail
summary: Lateral association is allowed only with a validation hook and a budget, otherwise it becomes context drift.

subject: logic
title: Natural language formalization
summary: Convert informal goals into claims, constraints, variables and obligations before proof or execution.

subject: logic
title: Proof obligation decomposition
summary: When a plan claims safety or correctness, list the obligations that must be shown or tested.

subject: logic
title: Counterexample-first check
summary: Search for a small counterexample before accepting a broad plan or cross-domain transfer.

subject: logic
title: Fact, assumption, plan and obligation layers
summary: Mark each statement as fact, assumption, plan or obligation so agents do not execute guesses as facts.

subject: logic
title: Temporal and invariant checks
summary: Long tasks need invariants and time-aware checkpoints to prevent drift and repeated mistakes.

subject: mathematics
title: Sets, relations and functions
summary: Basic set/relation/function thinking helps map graph nodes, edges, indexes and route transforms.

subject: mathematics
title: Common proof methods
summary: Direct proof, contradiction, induction and case analysis become lightweight engineering validation patterns.

subject: mathematics
title: Scoped graph search
summary: Use project_id, subject, route_id and task_id as filters before expanding graph neighborhoods.

subject: mathematics
title: Cost-aware route search
summary: Pick routes by expected value under context cost, execution risk and validation cost.

subject: mathematics
title: Metrics and statistical evaluation
summary: Use repeated scenarios and clear pass rates rather than anecdotal impressions to evaluate agent improvement.

subject: mathematics
title: FAME evidence update
summary: Use new evidence to update confidence, risk and usefulness rather than overwriting history.

subject: mathematics
title: Multi-objective tradeoff
summary: Balance correctness, speed, context cost, safety and learning value when choosing routes.

subject: computer-science
title: Complexity and resource budget
summary: Graph traversal and indexing must account for time, memory and token cost.

subject: computer-science
title: Requirements to acceptance criteria
summary: Turn vague implementation goals into behavior, constraints and verification commands.

subject: computer-science
title: Testing layers
summary: Use unit, integration, smoke, real-eval and release checks according to risk and blast radius.

subject: computer-science
title: Database schema and versioning
summary: Database-backed memory and asset stores need schemas, migrations, version fields and compatibility checks.

subject: computer-science
title: Inverted and semantic indexes
summary: Large knowledge nets need lexical and semantic indexes plus scoped filters to avoid graph explosion.

subject: computer-science
title: Light graph, heavy store
summary: Keep only preview and index refs in the graph; raw multimodal payloads and long text stay in stores.

subject: computer-science
title: Version control and traceable change
summary: Check dirty worktrees and preserve user changes before editing or packaging.

subject: computer-science
title: Secure development gate
summary: Release workflows should check secrets, unsafe defaults, exposed services and dependency risk.

subject: computer-science
title: Web platform knowledge entry
summary: Frontend work should connect UI behavior, accessibility, build artifacts and browser evidence.

subject: computer-science
title: Python runtime knowledge entry
summary: Agent scripts should verify interpreter, environment, module path, encoding and working directory.

subject: agent-tooling
title: ProposedAction risk statement
summary: Risk level determines whether the action is read-only, proposed, blocked or requires approval.

subject: agent-tooling
title: Tool result as evidence
summary: A result summary records exit state, key output, errors, artifacts and next verification.

subject: agent-tooling
title: Project memory overlay boundary
summary: Project memory informs future tasks but does not automatically pollute reusable core knowledge.

subject: agent-tooling
title: Agent scorecard
summary: Use stable metrics: tool success rate, context savings, repeated failure drop and user correction rate.

subject: powershell-safety
title: Output streams and redirection
summary: PowerShell streams and redirection behavior affect evidence capture and error diagnosis.

subject: agent-tooling
title: Filesystem scope
summary: Filesystem tools must declare working directory, allowed paths and expected side effects.

subject: agent-tooling
title: Git safety operations
summary: Do not reset, checkout or overwrite user changes without explicit approval; inspect status before edits.

subject: agent-tooling
title: Node/npm command boundary
summary: Confirm package root, script semantics and artifact side effects before npm commands.

subject: agent-tooling
title: Python runtime boundary
summary: Confirm interpreter, virtual environment, module path and working directory before Python execution.

subject: agent-tooling
title: Structured data edit safety
summary: Use parsers for JSON/JSONL and update indexes after edits.

subject: agent-tooling
title: Network download and external data import
summary: Record URL, date, license and purpose; unknown licenses remain links and summaries only.

subject: agent-tooling
title: Test and build evidence
summary: Do not claim completion without executing the relevant validation or explaining why it could not run.

subject: agent-tooling
title: Database and knowledge-net sync boundary
summary: Manual graph edits produce sync proposals for databases and asset indexes; review remains required.

subject: agent-tooling
title: Working directory confirmation
summary: Wrong working directory is a common failure signature; verify it before tool calls.

subject: language-tree-hub
title: Thinking layer selection
summary: Choose broad abstraction or narrow execution mode deliberately before graph traversal.

subject: language-tree-hub
title: Semantic adaptation and term normalization
summary: Normalize aliases, multilingual terms and tool names before route selection.

subject: language-tree-hub
title: Text directory index
summary: Provide an expandable subject directory synchronized with graph changes.

subject: agent-tooling
title: One-shot tool use
summary: Load tool manuals only when needed and retain only the resulting summary.

subject: agent-tooling
title: Self-set clock and reminder
summary: Use reminders and checkpoints to avoid task interruption and to resume from memory.

subject: agent-tooling
title: Mechanism enforcement
summary: Use checks, route decisions and gateway policies to make the workflow mandatory for agents.

subject: language-tree-hub
title: Goal gate backcasting
summary: Work backward from done criteria and evidence to the smallest route set.

subject: language-tree-hub
title: Global situation model
summary: Before action, hold goal, constraints, resources, risks, prior lessons and stop conditions together.

subject: agent-tooling
title: Tool action contract
summary: Every tool call needs tool, operation, scope, expected signal, validation, rollback and approval state.

subject: agent-tooling
title: High-frequency pitfall preflight
summary: Precheck common failure domains before execution.

subject: agent-tooling
title: Failure signature normalization
summary: Normalize recurring tool failures into signatures that can trigger recurrence guards.

subject: agent-tooling
title: External agent integration usability
summary: A useful plugin must be easy for agents to start, route, act and summarize without custom training.

subject: agent-tooling
title: Agent effect smoke scenarios
summary: Representative tasks show whether route, scope, preflight and summary mechanisms actually change behavior.

subject: agent-tooling
title: External agent ecosystem mapping
summary: Codex, Cursor, Claude, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI, Dify and generic agents can all map onto the same route/action/summary protocol.

title: Open-source practical bridge
summary: The open edition focuses on immediate wins: safer tool calls, better context control and clearer agent connection.

summary: When Chinese output looks wrong, verify console encoding, pipe decoding and UTF-8 file roundtrip before modifying files.

summary: The real evaluation verifies UTF-8 console/output settings and JSON file roundtrip with a Chinese probe string.

summary: External agents first separate MCP resources, prompts and tools; only tools may create external actions, and each tool must declare schema, permission, output shape and side effects.

summary: Each task receives only the minimum required tools, paths, network and database permissions; anything outside project, subject, route or allowed root must block or ask for approval.

summary: Sensitive tool calls are checked by guardrails and may pause for user approval or rejection, while preserving action id, approval state, block reason and resume point.

summary: Long tasks save thread_id, checkpoint_id, last stable evidence, blockers and the smallest next action; resuming reads summaries instead of replaying full logs.

summary: Engineering agents need stable repository observation, file navigation, editing, testing, error summaries and next-action interfaces instead of relying on model memory alone.

title: Repository navigation-edit-test loop
summary: Before code edits, locate package roots, test entries, related files and dirty worktree state; after edits, run risk-matched tests and summarize evidence.

summary: Open-source CI should limit default permissions, protect secrets, review third-party actions, pin release flow and treat security failures as release blockers.

subject: computer-science

summary: Portable zips, Docker images, release assets and install scripts must be traceable to source, build command, version, checks and license boundaries.

title: PowerShell native command boundary
summary: When invoking git, node, npm, python, docker or other native commands, confirm whether PowerShell pre-parses arguments and avoid opaque command strings.
